premises.text: Parking is a major urban problem that causes large shares of traffic as drivers circle for spots
Curb Karma is a smartphone social network where leavers publish spots and seekers reserve them with map, messaging, navigation, and ratings
premises.evidence_span: you can participate in a social network for parking

premises.text: Karma Credits mediate the exchange: seekers pay two credits, leavers earn one, and Curb Karma keeps one dollar of value
premises.evidence_span: Marissa needs two Karma Credits to reserve a spot

premises.text: The business targets high-demand urban spot exchanges and plans multi-city expansion of that take-rate model
premises.evidence_span: only about 50,000 of those are considered in high demand

domains.name: Karma Credit monetization and city market

value.text: Drivers find and reserve parking where and when they need it
value.evidence_span: Curb Karma finds you parking where and when you need it

causal_links.evidence_span: half of the traffic in Brooklyn is actually caused by people circling for a parking spot
Marissa can find and reserve Heather's parking spot

notes: Publish/reserve/map/message/nav/rate demo folded as one parking social-network cascade (§4.1.7). Karma Credit take-rate kept as commercial mechanism; high-demand exchange math as market premise for that model. Free credit promo treated as launch packaging. Anti-template: problem, app matching, and credit economics separately revisable.
